articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “She could have stopped me a long, long time ago, but she didn’t” - How Roger Federer turned a 22-year partnership with his wife Mirka into tennis perfection
articles.summary: International Sports News: Roger Federer’s career ended with 20 Grand Slam titles, eight Wimbledon trophies and 103 tour-level titles, but his final farewell was not really abou.
articles.body: Roger Federer’s career ended with 20 Grand Slam titles, eight Wimbledon trophies and 103 tour-level titles, but his final farewell was not really about the numbers. At the 2022 Laver Cup in London, Federer broke down while thanking his wife, Mirka Federer, for standing beside him through the hardest parts of his career. Their relationship began at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, when both were young tennis players. More than two decades later, Mirka was still beside him as he played his final match. Federer’s own words showed just how much that support meant to him.How did Roger Federer and Mirka Federer first meetRoger Federer and Miroslava “Mirka” Vavrinec met at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, where both represented Switzerland as tennis players. Federer was only 18 at the time, while Mirka was already competing on the professional circuit.Their meeting happened before Federer became the global tennis star that fans would later know. At that point, his career was still taking shape. Mirka, meanwhile, had her own ambitions in tennis and had competed at Grand Slam tournaments.Their lives changed when Mirka’s playing career was cut short by a foot injury in 2002. She had reached a career-high ranking of No. 76 in the WTA singles rankings, but the injury meant she could no longer continue competing at the same level.From there, Mirka remained closely connected to Federer’s tennis life. She became a familiar presence in his player box and travelled with him during a career that took the family around the world.Federer later married Mirka in 2009. Their partnership grew alongside his rise to the top of men’s tennis, giving their relationship a rare link to almost every stage of his professional career.What role did Mirka Federer play during Roger Federer’s careerIt would be too simple to describe Mirka Federer only as Roger Federer’s wife. She had been a professional tennis player herself, so she understood the demands of the sport from personal experience.As Federer’s career became more demanding, she stayed close to his daily life on tour. She was often seen watching from the stands and became part of the small family unit that travelled with him.Federer’s career eventually stretched across 24 years. He played more than 1,500 matches, spent 310 weeks at No. 1 and won 20 Grand Slam singles titles. The ATP Tour also records 103 tour-level trophies, numbers that show how long and demanding his career was.That long run also came with injuries, defeats and difficult decisions. Federer announced in September 2022 that the Laver Cup in London would be his final ATP event after repeated knee problems prevented him from returning to full competitive fitness.The most important point about Mirka’s role, however, came from Federer himself. He did not describe her support as something distant or ceremonial. Instead, he connected her directly to his ability to keep playing.How did Roger Federer describe Mirka Federer at his final matchFederer’s final professional match came on September 23, 2022, at the Laver Cup. He played doubles with Rafael Nadal against Jack Sock and Frances Tiafoe at London’s O2 Arena.The match ended in defeat, but the result quickly became secondary. Federer had already said the event would be his final ATP appearance, and after the match he became emotional while speaking about his family.Looking toward Mirka and their children, Federer said:“My wife has been so supportive… She could have stopped me a long, long time ago, but she didn’t. She kept me going and allowed me to play. It’s amazing. Thank you.”The words mattered because they came at the end of a career that had demanded years of travel, training and recovery. Federer was not simply thanking Mirka for being present at one final match. He was recognising the support that had continued through the many years before it.He also thanked his parents, Robert and Lynette, during the farewell. His family had been courtside for the emotional ending, making the moment much more personal than a normal retirement ceremony.Federer later spoke about the evening as a “perfect journey” and said he would do it all over again. The ATP Tour reported that Mirka, their children and Federer’s parents were all watching from courtside as his professional career came to an end.Why does Roger Federer and Mirka Federer’s story still stand outFederer and Mirka’s story stands out because their partnership grew while his tennis life was becoming increasingly demanding. They met when Federer was still a young player. They married before he completed much of his record-breaking career, and Mirka remained part of his life through his biggest wins and his eventual retirement.The couple also raised four children: twin daughters Myla and Charlene, followed by twin sons Leo and Lenny. Their family life developed alongside Federer’s international career, which required constant travel and long periods away from home.There are several quotes often shared online about Federer’s family life, including claims that he “could not sleep without my wife” and that Mirka “made that nomadic life feel like a real home for our children everywhere we went.” Another widely circulated quote has Federer saying:“When I met her, I had zero titles. Today I have over 100. She’s been with me through every single victory and every defeat. She built my schedule, packed our bags, and took care of everything so I could just focus on playing the game I loved.”Those longer quotes could not be independently verified in reliable primary or major sports sources during this fact-check. For that reason, they should not be presented as confirmed Federer remarks. His farewell comments about Mirka, however, were directly recorded after his final match and are well documented.That distinction matters. Federer’s real words were already powerful enough. He had spent years collecting trophies and records, yet when the moment came to speak about the people who helped him through the journey, his attention went to his wife, children and parents.His final tribute to Mirka also explains why their relationship remains an important part of Federer’s story. His career was built on extraordinary tennis, but it was not lived by him alone.Federer finished with 20 Grand Slam singles titles, including eight at Wimbledon, and retired as one of the defining players of his generation. Yet his farewell showed another side of that career: the person waiting beyond the court, supporting him while the cameras focused on the champion.For Federer, Mirka was not simply watching the journey. She was part of it. And when he finally said goodbye to professional tennis, he made sure the world knew it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
